newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up to 11.5 from 10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up to 11.5 from 10.9 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.5 percent on Friday from 10.9 percent.

A total of 20.7 million kuna were settled, leaving 10.3 million surplus on the supply side. Demand stood at 31 million kuna, but was not entirely met as lenders and borrowers failed to agree on terms.
The rates for fresh interbank borrowings ranged between 10 percent for call money and 13 percent for one-month funds.
Some 5.5 million old loans were rolled over by insurers and banks at 10 to 14 percent, depending on length.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and next Monday weaker at 5.7066 from 5.6510 against the dollar and 3.5617 from 3.5570 against the mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
